inconsistencies: #32554 and #36254 address the same defect (BlockToJsonVerbosity3 benchmarking nothing without undo data). #36254 is the minimal fix and should be reviewed first; #32554 is the larger fixture-replacement approach (itself superseding #32457) and the two should not both land unexamined.
#35139 and #35713 both introduce in-tree assertion macros to replace Boost.Test. Review #35713 first as the full runner replacement; #35139 risks duplicating its framework if merged independently.
Chain: #36091 adds the operator<< stringification that #35713 needs for readable failures; it should be reviewed before or together with #35713 even though it sits a band lower.
#34969 and #36068 are both wallet-fuzz throughput optimizations by the same author touching overlapping harness code; reviewing them together avoids conflicting rewrites.
#36437 explicitly unblocks the follow-up orphanage hole fixes in #36506, which is why it leads the category despite being filed as test work.
#35356 is gated on the wallet_signer.py path-quoting bug it exposes; the ordering only makes sense if that fix lands first (the fix is not itself in this category).
#35442 bundles and depends on #35433 (RBF argument deprecation), outside this category; its band here reflects only the test-side cleanup.
#36074 and #36087 are two halves of the same assertion-hygiene effort; if both are taken, review them in that order to avoid repeated scripted-diff churn.
#32409 is effectively dead work (NACKed, unused in CI) rather than merely low priority; consider closing instead of queueing for review.
result.notes: No P1 in this category: nothing here leaves a correctness or reliability problem unresolved for a release cycle on its own; the strongest items are the orphanage liveness fix with its harness, consensus-level unit coverage, and the Boost.Test runner replacement, all solid P2. The P2 set was kept to the two flaky-CI fixes plus the four pieces of durable framework/coverage infrastructure; the long tail of new fuzz targets, benchmarks and static test vectors is genuinely similar in consequence and shares P3, ordered by breadth of the code path they reach.
